obligations.note: The change sets payments PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES and controls/payments/policy-params.json payments.privileged_idle_minutes to 16. The catalog bound is payments.privileged_idle_minutes <= 15, and no valid exception covers the deviation.
The cited exception EXC-0253 is scoped to component mortgage.session, not payments.session. The only payments.session exception, EXC-0141, expired on 2026-09-23, before the 2026-10-23 review time.
Ticket CHG-26241 is standard and was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-16, before the change opened. Its components (payments.controls-data, payments.policy) cover both changed files.
Mara Costa, a change_approver for payments and not the author, gave a code_review approval on the head commit.
Both approvals name the single head commit e650d922, and there are no later commits.

run.json reports success on the head commit from ci-runner-02, started 2026-10-17. The attached JUnit report, however, is timestamped 2026-10-23 and came from host dev-laptop-7.local, so it is not shown to be that run's output. Its passing SES-1 control test is also inconsistent with a 16-minute value.
Only payments.policy and payments.controls-data are touched; neither is marked security_sensitive, so no security review is required.
The protected controls/payments/policy-params.json changed. Bao Tran (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's payments-eng team) approved the head commit.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not an emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers payments policy.py PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES or policy-params, so no earlier evidence lapses through this change.

summary: The change raises the payments privileged session idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes, which violates SES-1's approved bound of at most 15. The risk acceptance cited in the change request, EXC-0253, is scoped to mortgage.session rather than payments.session. The only payments session exception, EXC-0141, has expired. The CI evidence is also questionable: the JUnit report came from a local workstation on a later date than the recorded run. Because SES-1 and EXC-1 are refuted, the change is rejected.
